verdict_reason: The research Skill has a clear source-targeting scenario, strong evidence-first workflow, and useful report structure, but two P1 defects remain in deterministic/runtime formal-completion enforcement. Team use should stay conditional until the report completion gate is registered and the gate checks the Skill's own Report Self-Review and User Confirmation requirements.

dimension_scores.reason: The Skill names the team-use scenario before external information becomes action, defines the target object and source-targeting problem, and specifies a Decision Package consumer in shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:15, shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:34, and shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:128.

The body has good adjacent routing for lightweight answers, deep-research, and github-repo-radar in shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:47-54 and shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:80-84, but the source OpenAI adapter allows implicit invocation while the runtime surface says research is manual.

Most critical sentences are executable: the hard gates specify stop conditions, the core contracts define objects and outputs, and references have retrieval triggers. The weakest critical path is formal completion because deterministic enforcement does not match the prose gate.

The workflow order is causal: routing and target definition feed source targeting, evidence qualification feeds judgment calibration, and judgment feeds the decision package in shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:60-68.

The Decision Package and formal report template give downstream consumers usable outputs, but formal report handoff is weakened because the current deterministic check accepts reports without the required self-review and confirmation gate.

The package has scripts, retain evidence, and focused tests, but the formal completion gate is not registered in the hook registry and the script/test fixture do not enforce the Skill's own Report Self-Review and User Confirmation requirements.

Runtime installation can apply the runtime-surface contract, but the source adapter conflicts with the manual runtime entry, and the research completion script is not present in shared/hooks/registry.json skill_completion_gates.

Target prompts, evals, lifecycle evidence, retain evidence, and focused research gates exist and pass, but those gates miss the runtime registration and formal-completion validation defects found in this audit.

The Skill is concise, reference routes have consumers, and the report template consolidates split projections. The remaining noise is not volume; it is duplicated completion truth spread across prose, template, script, tests, and runtime registry.

findings.title: Formal report completion gate is not registered in the runtime hook registry
findings.evidence: shared/skills/research/SKILL.md:24 requires formal research completion to wait for report, self-review, and user confirmation; shared/skills/research/scripts/completion_check.sh:3 says the trigger is research skill-local Stop; shared/hooks/registry.json:3 defines the active skill_completion_gates list and shared/hooks/registry.json:289 closes the listed gates without a research entry. The independent probe printed registry_has_research_gate= False.

evidence_checks.expected_snippet: Do NOT call formal research complete until `docs/{feature}/research-report.md` exists, Report Self-Review passes, and the user confirms the report.
evidence_checks.claim: The target Skill requires a formal completion gate before completion can be claimed.

required_claims: Formal research completion is supposed to be gated before the Skill can be called complete.
The research completion_check script exists and presents itself as the research Stop gate.
The active hook registry is the runtime source for skill completion gates.
The active hook registry has no research entry.
claim_review.refutation_check: install.sh:1139 injects Claude skill hooks from the registry, and shared/hooks/registry.json:3 is the checked registry list; no direct refutation or separate research hook registration was found in the active runtime surfaces.

severity_calibration.team_use_impact: A team can believe formal research completion is runtime-gated while installed runtimes do not dispatch the target completion check, allowing incomplete research reports to pass handoff without deterministic enforcement.
severity_calibration.rationale: This is P1 because it affects runtime validation and downstream handoff correctness. It is not P0 because the Skill prose still instructs the agent to self-gate and focused static tests exist, so the defect does not by itself make every research use unsafe.

findings.impact: A team can believe formal research completion is runtime-gated while installed runtimes do not dispatch the target completion check, allowing incomplete research reports to pass handoff without deterministic enforcement.
findings.repair_target: shared/hooks/registry.json plus any hook-rendering tests that assert research completion gate registration
findings.verification_hint: Register the research completion gate or explicitly retire the script from runtime claims; then run a focused install/runtime or hook-registry test proving research appears in skill_completion_gates and is dispatched.

claim_review.refutation_check: shared/skills/research/scripts/completion_check.sh:92 begins the section-order checks for shared appendix/profile sections, but no checked line in the script requires Report Self-Review or User Confirmation Gate; the valid fixture pass assertion at tests/test-research-skill-contract.sh:211 remains the strongest active refutation check and supports the finding.

severity_calibration.team_use_impact: Formal research artifacts can pass the deterministic contract without the self-review and confirmation state that downstream teams rely on before accepting or handing off a judgment.
severity_calibration.rationale: This is P1 because it can mislead output readiness and downstream handoff. It is not P0 because it is repairable in the completion script and tests without changing the research methodology itself.

findings.impact: Formal research artifacts can pass the deterministic contract without the self-review and confirmation state that downstream teams rely on before accepting or handing off a judgment.
findings.verification_hint: Extend completion_check.sh to require Report Self-Review and User Confirmation Gate evidence for formal reports, update valid/invalid fixtures, then rerun bash tests/test-research-skill-contract.sh and bash tests/run-focused.sh research.

findings.title: Source OpenAI adapter allows implicit invocation despite manual runtime surface
findings.evidence: shared/skills/research/agents/openai.yaml:7 sets allow_implicit_invocation: true, while contracts/skill-runtime-surface.json:308-312 marks research as manual because research workflows are broad and potentially high-cost. install.sh:2191-2193 requires manual skills to disable implicit invocation, and tools/skills/apply_skill_runtime_surface.py:169-203 can self-heal runtime copies.
findings.impact: The source package presents a routing policy that contradicts the active runtime contract. Maintainers or direct adapter consumers can treat research as auto-routable even though the repo's runtime surface says it should be explicit.
findings.repair_target: shared/skills/research/agents/openai.yaml or the adapter-generation path that owns source OpenAI policy
findings.verification_hint: Align the source adapter with the manual runtime surface or document why source adapters are intentionally generated differently; then run the Codex runtime surface tests that check manual implicit-invocation policy.

repair_handoff.action: Register research completion_check as an active completion gate or remove runtime-gate claims from the research script and Skill contract.
Make formal report validation require Report Self-Review and User Confirmation Gate evidence, and update valid/invalid fixtures accordingly.
Align source adapter implicit-invocation policy with the manual runtime surface or document the source/runtime generation split.
